judgments.justification: The listed Method M values “1.2e-4,” “2.8e-4,” “7.0e-4,” and “6.6e-6” are below 0.001 for all four benchmarks.
It explicitly states “lower p-values than PaCoST and LLM DI on all four benchmarks” and supplies both LLM DI variants’ values.
It reports lower full-method p-values and one benchmark example, but omits the ablations’ different significance patterns across all four benchmarks.
“All p-values on the uncontaminated model and on held-out subsets…exceeded 0.05” correctly covers both false-positive settings.
It notes “no statistical tests or repeated runs are reported” and appropriately limits the reliability of the observed differences.
The complete p-value lists “on all four benchmarks” encode the stated significance pattern for PaCoST, both LLM DI variants, and Method M.
“P-values below 0.001 on all four benchmarks” directly reports successful detection for TriviaQA, ARC-C, MMLU, and GSM8K.
It says baselines were above 0.05 on most benchmarks, but does not establish that Method M was lower for every baseline-benchmark comparison.
Neither ablation nor its benchmark-specific significance pattern is discussed.
“Did not flag data the model never saw” covers both settings; the misstated 0.15 minimum remains above 0.05 and does not reverse the finding.
“Limited to a single model…single training run” and “no statistical tests” communicates the required limitation on comparative reliability.
The broad statement that baselines exceeded 0.05 “on most benchmarks” omits the distinct significance pattern for each baseline variant.
The listed Method M values “1.2e-4,” “2.8e-4,” “7.0e-4,” and “6.6e-6” are below 0.001 for all four benchmarks.
It explicitly states “lower p-values than PaCoST and LLM DI on all four benchmarks” and supplies both LLM DI variants’ values.
It reports lower full-method p-values and one benchmark example, but omits the ablations’ different significance patterns across all four benchmarks.
“All p-values on the uncontaminated model and on held-out subsets…exceeded 0.05” correctly covers both false-positive settings.
It notes “no statistical tests or repeated runs are reported” and appropriately limits the reliability of the observed differences.
The complete p-value lists “on all four benchmarks” encode the stated significance pattern for PaCoST, both LLM DI variants, and Method M.
“P-values below 0.001 on all four benchmarks” directly reports successful detection for all four intentionally included benchmarks.
It does not state or provide enough values to show Method M was lower than every baseline variant on every benchmark.
The full method’s ablations are not discussed.
It claims Abstracts at “0.07…fell below the conventional 0.05 threshold”; 0.07 is above 0.05, so every held-out result was non-significant.
“Limited to a single model…single training run” and “no statistical tests” communicates the required limitation on comparative reliability.
It identifies LLM DI-different’s two detections but does not report PaCoST’s sole detection or that LLM DI-same never detected contamination.
